thr.explain: Auto-calibration runs after a model switch and on “Calibrate”: it puts the threshold above the background noise of the scene, never above the confirmed passes. It cannot tell how many people are missed (recall) without labelled people — if a camera misses passes, set its threshold manually.

scan.inactive: 🔐 New Hikvision cameras without a password (not activated): {count}. Activation sets the admin password on the camera — it cannot be undone without a reset button.
act.confirm:
⚠️ Activate {count} camera(s): {hosts}.
Activation is irreversible: the admin password can only be removed by a factory reset on the camera itself. One password is set on every camera of the batch.
To continue, send the word «{word}». Anything else cancels.
act.cancelled: Activation cancelled — the cameras were not touched.
act.ask_password:
🔑 Send the admin password for these cameras: 8–16 Latin characters, at least two groups out of digits, lowercase, uppercase and symbols, no spaces, without the word admin.
Or send «{word}» — a strong password will be generated.
I will delete the message right after reading it; the password is shown to the owner once, privately, after a successful activation.

act.password_charset: Only Latin letters, digits and symbols, no spaces.
act.password_weak: Too weak: the camera requires at least two groups — digits, lowercase, uppercase, symbols.
act.password_has_user: The password must not contain the user name admin.
act.password_rules: I have deleted the message — send another password or «generate». The cameras were not touched.

scan.manual: 🛠 Cameras waiting for first-time setup: {count}. The bot cannot set their first password automatically yet (auto-activation is Hikvision-only) — do it by hand, it takes a couple of minutes.
scan.manual_next: Once a password is set and RTSP/ONVIF is on, tap the camera's button — I will ask for the login and password. Or tap “Search again”.
setup.generic: Open the camera address in a browser (http://address): a new camera offers to set the administrator password itself. If the page does not open, use the vendor's discovery tool or app. Then enable ONVIF (or RTSP) in the network settings and create an ONVIF user if asked.
setup.hikvision: Hikvision/HiWatch: this camera did not answer the activation request, so there is no button. Open http://address in a browser (Activation window) or use SADPTool / Hik-Connect and set the admin password. Then: Configuration → Network → Advanced → Integration → enable ONVIF and add a user.
setup.dahua: Dahua: open http://address in a browser — the Device Initialization wizard asks for the admin password and a reset e-mail; ConfigTool (Initialize) or the DMSS app do the same. ONVIF is off on newer firmware: Network → Platform Access / ONVIF → enable, authentication with your login and password.
setup.imou: Imou: these cameras are set up in the Imou Life app (QR code on the body); the device password is the safety code on the label or the one set in the app. For RTSP/ONVIF enable local access/ONVIF in the app; login admin, password that code.
setup.uniview: Uniview: open http://address in a browser — newer firmware asks to set the admin password (older: admin/123456, change it right away); in bulk use EZTools (Activate) or the EZView app. ONVIF: Setup → Network → Port/ONVIF, authentication Digest.
setup.tantos: Tantos ships cameras on several platforms. Find the camera with the TANTOS camera search tool; older TSi models log in as admin/admin — change the password right away. If the web UI (http://address) shows an Activation window, follow the Hikvision way (SADP); Initialization means the Dahua way (ConfigTool). Then enable ONVIF and create a user.
setup.axis: Axis (AXIS OS 10+): there is no default password. Open http://address — the wizard asks to create the first administrator (user and password); AXIS IP Utility / Device Manager can do it too. RTSP works right away with that account; create an ONVIF user under System → Users → ONVIF.
setup.hanwha: Hanwha Vision (Wisenet): there is no default password — on first login at http://address the camera requires an admin password; in bulk use Wisenet Device Manager. Then check in the network settings that RTSP and ONVIF are on and use that account.
setup.reolink: Reolink: set the password in the Reolink app or Reolink Client (the camera shows up among LAN devices). On newer models HTTP, RTSP and ONVIF stay off afterwards: Network → Advanced → Server/Port Settings → enable RTSP, ONVIF and HTTP.
setup.vigi: TP-Link VIGI: there is no default password. Activate it in the VIGI app, VIGI Security Manager (Discovered Devices → Add) or at https://address — the camera asks to set the admin password. ONVIF works with that account on port 2020, RTSP on 554.
setup.ezviz: EZVIZ: a cloud camera without a local wizard. Add it in the EZVIZ app; the RTSP password is the verification code on the label, login admin. RTSP is enabled in the app: LAN Live View → Local Server Settings. Not every model has ONVIF.
setup.milesight: Milesight: firmware V4x.7.0.69 and newer requires activation — open http://address or Smart Tools (status Inactive → Activate), set the password and security questions. Older firmware logs in as admin/ms1234 — change it right away. Then check that ONVIF is on.
setup.tvt: TVT: open http://address or the IPTool utility — a new camera shows an Activation window (8–16 character password); older firmware logs in as admin/123456 — change it right away. Then enable ONVIF in the camera's network settings.
setup.xiongmai: Xiongmai (XMEye/NetSurveillance): the initial account is admin with an empty password, or a password wizard in the XMEye app / DeviceManager tool. Set a password right away (these cameras are often hijacked), enable ONVIF in network settings and block internet access if you do not need the cloud.
setup.ajax: Ajax: the camera has no local password — it works only within an Ajax system. Add it in the Ajax app, then enable ONVIF integration in the camera settings and create an ONVIF user: the camera is added here with that login and password.
